rounds.proof_sketch: Input shape [16, 16384] has size = 262144 elements. The scalar kernel (containing the mutation) is only invoked when size < 1024. Since 262144 >= 1024, the vectorized kernel is always used instead. The mutated line in hardsigmoid_kernel_scalar is never executed.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes threadIdx.x to threadIdx.y on line 48 of the hardsigmoid_kernel_scalar kernel. However, this kernel is only called when the input tensor has fewer than 1024 elements (see the conditional: 'if (size >= 1024) { use vectorized } else { use scalar }'). The fixed input shape is [16, 16384], which contains 262144 elements. Since 262144 >> 1024, the code always takes the vectorized kernel path, and the scalar kernel containing the mutation is never executed. No value-level changes can alter which kernel is selected since that decision depends solely on tensor size (number of elements), which is fixed by the shape contract.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed-shape contract. The mutation resides in the scalar kernel path which is only triggered for tensors with fewer than 1024 elements. The fixed input shape of [16, 16384] = 262144 elements always triggers the vectorized kernel path. To kill this mutant would require changing the input shape to have fewer than 1024 elements, which violates the testing contract.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing frameworks should detect when mutations occur in code paths that are unreachable under fixed input configurations. The kernel selection logic based on tensor size creates distinct code paths - mutations in the scalar kernel path cannot be tested when input sizes always exceed the threshold. Consider either: (1) testing with multiple input sizes, or (2) flagging such mutants as 'configuration-dependent equivalent' to avoid false positives in mutation scores.
